definition: Feedback neural networks are neural networks with the ability to provide bottom-up and top-down design feedback to their input or previous layers, based on their outputs or subsequent layers.
details: This is notably used in large language models, specifically in reasoning language models (RLM). This process is designed to mimic self-assessment and internal deliberation, aiming to minimize errors (like hallucinations) and increase interpretability. This reflection is a form of "test-time compute", where additional computational resources are used during inference.
